key_insight: Can human forecasters’ written discussions improve tropical cyclone intensity predictions beyond numerical weather data? This study investigates that question across 637 storms; the provided abstract is truncated and does not report the results.
problem_solved: Determining whether National Hurricane Center discussions contain useful predictive information beyond standard numerical inputs for forecasting tropical cyclone intensity.
method: Analyze Tropical Cyclone Discussions for 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific storms from the 2002–2023 hurricane seasons.
Combine discussion text with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields.
Assess the added predictive value of discussion text beyond the numerical inputs.
impact: The study addresses a practical multimodal ML question: whether expert-written text adds information beyond structured and spatial weather data. Its findings could inform how forecasting systems incorporate human expertise, although the supplied excerpt does not establish an improvement.
visual_elements: Three-input diagram: forecaster discussion text, SHIPS environmental predictors, and ERA5 wind fields feeding an intensity prediction system.
Atlantic and eastern North Pacific map labeled with 637 tropical cyclones and the 2002–2023 study period.
Side-by-side comparison schematic: numerical inputs only versus numerical inputs plus discussion text.
Annotated discussion excerpt illustrating the expert narrative being evaluated.
paper_title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
paper_authors: Ilia Azizi, Frederick Iat-Hin Tam, Marc-Olivier Boldi, Valérie Chavez-Demoulin, Tom Beucler
